text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien has settled on a sweeping cabinet shuffle that leaves his overall economic direction intact, Canadian television reports said on Tuesday.
Chretien's Liberals won re-election June 2, and he was due to announce the cabinet for his second term Wednesday.
The reports by the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation (CBC) and CTV News confirmed news already reported by Reuters that Chretien would reappoint Finance Minister Paul Martin.

Martin had set the tone for the first 3-1/2-year term by slashing virtually every department's budget to restore Canada's international financial respectability, and made it clear Canada must stay the course until its budget deficit is gone.
And, despite pleas by some members of the Liberal caucus for a more leftist slant after all the cuts, one of the leading leftists in the cabinet, Sheila Copps, will be demoted.
Copps will be replaced as deputy prime minister by the staid veteran Herb Gray, the reports said.

She will maintain her position as Canadian Heritage minister, where she has defended protection of Canadian cultural industries. But she will be kept out of the health portfolio, expected to be a juicy department if as expected Canada moves into a budget surplus.

The networks said Justice Minister Allan Rock, who tightened gun control and widened homosexual rights, would take over at health. He will be replaced by Natural Resources Minister Anne McLellan, an Albertan who was widely respected by her province's energy industry.

Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale, one of few Liberals remaining in the Western provinces, will replace her while retaining responsibility for the Canadian Wheat Board monopoly, and House Agriculture Committee Chairman Lyle Vanclief of Ontario will replace him.
Ontario is the largest agricultural producing province, but the Western provinces are the biggest farm exporters, with many farmers clamouring for the right to sell their grain on the free market.
Trade Minister Art Eggleton moves over to defence, replacing acid-tongued Doug Young, who was not re-elected, and Environment Minister Sergio Marchi takes over at trade.

David Collenette, who had earlier resigned under a cloud as defence minister, becomes transport minister, replacing British Columbia's David Anderson, who goes to fisheries in the midst of a Pacific salmon dispute with the United States.
John Manley, on the right wing of the cabinet, retains the powerful position of industry minister and Lloyd Axworthy stays as foreign minister, the reports said.
Over them all, effectively, is Finance Minister Martin, keenly aware that any major deviation from his budget plans could well throttle the financial markets.
